summary: Read all 40 published pages against all 43 accepted items, 19 prerequisites, five routes, the reader and independent review. Four findings: two high (unrestricted formal étaleness and a negative-weight counterexample to the bad-operator bound), two medium (a false product-map helper in the quasi-compactness proof and an already planned finiteness criterion marked missing). These concern the exported statements and planning frontier; the corrected hypotheses suffice for the intended classicality argument. The 14 previously confirmed sourceIssues are credited rather than reported again.

findings.claim: Item 7 asserts that the algebraic morphism P from the integral PEL model to the BT stack is formally étale without restricting to p-nilpotent bases. It is false on characteristic-zero infinitesimal thickenings. Item 6's correct p-nilpotence restriction is not carried into this derived assertion.
findings.evidence: Published §1.3, p.984, writes the unrestricted P and calls it 'formellement étale'; Katz, Serre–Tate local moduli, Theorem 1.2.1, printed p.143, explicitly assumes p nilpotent in the base ring. Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field K, finite étale group schemes, and hence p-divisible groups with their compatible levels, lift uniquely across K[ε]/(ε²)→K. Elliptic curves do not: for E_t:y²=x(x−1)(x−t), j(t)=256(t²−t+1)³/(t²(1−t)²), and j'(3)=31360/27≠0. Thus t=3+ε gives a nontrivial first-order deformation with the same lifted BT group. Polarization and prime-to-p level do not remove this example. P is not even formally unramified there.
findings.fix: Keep the algebraic construction of P and the Iwahori fiber product. Restrict its formal-étaleness assertion to p-locally-nilpotent test schemes, equivalently the relevant p-adic formal completions with their fixed dimension/signature components. Import this restricted Serre–Tate theorem from AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4. Add a sourceIssue for the missing qualification on p.984 and propagate the qualification into item 7, the reader and the Part II brief.

findings.claim: The bad-operator norm bound is exported for every dominant integral weight, but replacing the actual degree by a lower bound requires a nonnegative minimum weight. For negative minimum weight the claimed inequality can fail, not merely become unproved.
findings.evidence: Published Lemma 4.4.5, p.1004, only assumes “deg L ≥ ν”; the weight domain on p.994 allows all dominant GL-weights. In type C take F0=Q, a1=2, d1=n=1, κ=(-1,-1) and an ordinary étale Iwahori flag. Its canonical multiplicative complement L=μ_p² has degree 2 and gives a single branch. Katz Lemma 4.1.3, printed p.170, gives canonical-isogeny pullback p on invariant differentials, hence p² on det ω and p^(-2) on det ω^(-1). BPS §2.3 normalizes this branch by p^(-3); on integral local trivializations its operator norm is p^5. The permitted lower bound ν=1 instead predicts p^(3−1·(-1))=p^4. The same sign-sensitive replacement is explicit in Bijakowski v2, Lemma 3.15 proof, pp.22–23.
findings.fix: State the degree-lower-bound version with c_i≥0, where c_i is min_j k_{i,j,a_i} in type C or min_j(k_{i,j,a_i}+l_{i,j,b_i}) in type A; otherwise retain actual partial degrees with their signed weights rather than substitute ν. Add a sourceIssue identifying the missing sign condition in Lemma 4.4.5 and update item 28, reader and Part II brief. In the classicality application explicitly discharge positivity using Hypothesis 4.5.1 and the nonnegative eigenvalue valuations stated on p.994. This repairs the exported lemma without changing the intended small-slope theorem.

findings.claim: The extraction leaves unmarked a false helper assertion in the proof of Lemma 4.4.3: the map q:B_k^0→(X_Iw^rig)^k of simultaneous quotients is not étale for k≥2 on positive-dimensional moduli. A blueprint following the accepted source would be asked to prove an impossible helper.
findings.evidence: Published p.1003 says 'p et q sont finis et étales'. The domain B_k^0 is an open in a finite étale cover of X_Iw^rig and has dimension D, while the target product has dimension kD. For genus-two Siegel moduli D=3 and k=2 with two distinct complements, the dimensions are 3 and 6, ruling out étaleness. The predecessor's Lemma 2.20, PDF p.18, repeats the assertion. The desired quasi-compactness conclusion has a repair: each coordinate quotient map from the full B_k^rig factors through the finite étale forgetful map to C_i^rig and p2; §2.2, pp.989–990, supplies finiteness of both correspondence projections.
findings.fix: Add a sourceIssue for the proof helper and attach it to item 27 and its design obligation. Work on E12's closed quasi-compact degree boxes. On the full B_k^rig pull back V_l separately along each finite coordinate map, intersect these finitely many quasi-compact opens with p^(-1)(U), and apply the finite étale p-image result (Proposition 4.1.4). Separatedness supplies quasi-separatedness for the intersections. Do not assert that the product map is étale or that restriction to an arbitrary open preserves its finiteness. Preserve Lemma 4.4.3 and Theorem 4.4.1 with this repaired argument.

findings.claim: The finiteness criterion of Proposition 4.1.8 is marked missing although the current integrated atlas already plans the stronger Conrad criterion at AdicSpacesPartII:R2/fibral-finiteness-criterion. The route is in the correct roadmap, but its missing frontier would commission an already owned theorem.
findings.evidence: data/decompositions/AdicSpacesPartII.json, node AdicSpacesPartII:R2/fibral-finiteness-criterion, states and decomposes Conrad A.1.2: a flat rigid map is finite iff “quasi-compact and separated with finite fibers” and its fiber rank is locally constant. Read the source at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/papers/genpaper.pdf, pp.37–39 (matching accepted hash ab6daecb…). For g=f|U in item 21, étaleness supplies flatness, the quasi-compact open immersion and finite f supply quasi-compactness, and the constant geometric fiber cardinality equals the fiber rank. Thus A.1.2 makes g finite. The open U is then also closed in X (its map to the separated finite Y-space X is proper), and the complement is finite étale. These are applications of the existing R2 criterion and R0 finite/étale API, not a new missing finiteness theorem.
